[THOUGHT] A rapidly growing (weeks) 2-cm dome-shaped forehead lesion with a central keratin plug in a 67-year-old on sun-exposed skin is most consistent with keratoacanthoma. Differential includes well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma (can have keratinous core) and less likely nodular BCC, but the speed of growth and classic central crater strongly favor keratoacanthoma. Definitive management requires excisional biopsy and histopathology to exclude invasive SCC.

[DIAGNOSIS] Keratoacanthoma (likely)
